modeling_notes: Messages are sent in plaintext, matching the reviewed protocol where no encryption is applied.
No long-term keys are present; consequently, the adversary can learn the session key by intercepting both nonces ~na and ~nb.
Role B checks for the expected 'ACK' string before installing the session key and completing, as specified.
Secrecy lemmas are expected to produce counterexamples because kdf(~na,~nb) is derivable by the adversary from the public nonces.
The exists-trace lemma relies on a single parallel composition of A and B to witness both RoleDone events.
expected_limitations: The executability lemma is satisfied with a single session trace; replication is unnecessary for this target.
The secrecy lemmas are expected to be falsified, confirming that the protocol offers no secrecy under the Dolev-Yao adversary.
The field review flag for compromise.reveal_events is irrelevant because there are no long-term keys to reveal.
